title: Introduce Thrifty Defaults Pipeline and Quant 'Taste Test' For Safe Unit‑Econ Rollouts
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Adds a telemetry-driven defaults pipeline and lightweight quality 'taste test' to validate quant profiles before tenant rollout. Exposes CLI for dry-run and export. No breaking API changes.
description: Context: Customers asked for safer, automated defaults that reduce per-token cost without surprising quality regressions. Motivation: We need an automated pipeline that converts sampled workload telemetry into tenant-specific batching, cache, and quantization recommendations while running a fast quality safety check prior to rollout. Summary: This PR introduces the 'Thrifty Defaults Pipeline' and a lightweight quant 'Taste Test' harness. The pipeline ingests sample traces, computes candidate default bundles (batch shape, cache TTLs, quant profile suggestions), and outputs a ranked set of defaults with estimated unit-econ deltas. The 'Taste Test' runs a small, deterministic eval set with multiple quant candidates and reports quality delta metrics (ROUGE/EMB cosine/response-length divergence) alongside cost estimates so operators can set safe thresholds. What changed (high-level): 1) pkg/defaults/pipeline: new pipeline orchestration and scheduler for running nightly generation jobs, accepts workload-sample artifacts and tenant profiles. 2) pkg/defaults/curators: heuristics and ranking logic for batching/cache/quant bundles. 3) tools/thriftyctl: CLI to run dry-runs, export candidate bundles as YAML, and create preview rollouts. 4) infra/telemetry/bridge: lightweight adapter to synthesize sampling artifacts from existing trace events. 5) tests/e2e/taste_test: deterministic test harness plus a small synthetic workload to validate behavior. Commits: - 9f8a1fc: initial pipeline scaffold and scheduler interface. - b2c3d4e: add curator heuristics for batch/cache/quant ranking and scoring. - c4d5e6f: implement thriftctl CLI and export paths. - a7b8c9d: telemetry bridge and synthetic sample converter. - d1e2f3a: taste-test harness and metric reporter. - e4f5g6h: unit tests, e2e scenario, and documentation. Changed files (examples): - pkg/defaults/pipeline/pipeline.go - pkg/defaults/curators/ranker.go - tools/thriftyctl/main.go - infra/telemetry/bridge/convert.go - tests/e2e/taste_test/test_runner.go - docs/operations/thrifty-defaults.md - charts/defaults-generator/values.yaml - ci/recipes/taste-test-dockerfile - pkg/metrics/recipes/cost-estimator.go Review conversation: Jared Cole: "Can the taste test be configured to run on a per-tenant eval set rather than the synthetic one? Concerned about edge cases where synthetic samples miss distributional quirks." Priya Menon: "Yes, the CLI already accepts a --tenant-eval-path flag and the pipeline will prioritize tenant-sourced evals when present; added docs and an integration test to cover that flow in e2e." Aisha Rahman: "Please add guardrails so we never auto-rollout a quant that regresses >X% on any key metric." Priya Menon: "Added an explicit safety gate in the curator that rejects candidates exceeding thresholds configured in infra/telemetry/bridge/safety.yaml. Also added a dry-run mode that outputs a human-readable rejection rationale." Miguel Alvarez (nit): "Minor logging clarity request in ranker.go" Priya Menon: "Addressed; improved logs and added a comment explaining the scoring buckets." CI notes: Initial pipeline check failed lint on tools/thriftyctl (go vet); fixed in b2c3d4e and reran. Integration job ran the e2e taste test in a containerized runner, reported cost deltas and quality metrics and passed thresholds. All checks green at merge. Migration/ rollout plan: Nightly generator runs in staging for 2 weeks, outputs candidate bundles to staging S3 prefix. Operators may run thriftyctl preview --tenant <id> to inspect. After telemetry stability and manual signoff, defaults can be promoted to production with thriftyctl promote --bundle <id>. Rollback: bundles are immutable and previous defaults are stored per-tenant; promote action includes a built-in rollback window and automated revert if runtime errors spike (monitored by existing alerts). Observability: New metrics pref_defaults.generated_count, taste_test.quality_delta, taste_test.cost_delta. Dashboards added under Redwood Console > Defaults Generator. Backwards compatibility: No runtime API changes; defaults are consumed by existing serving config layer and considered opt-in until promoted. Risks and mitigations: Risk: misaligned tenant evals may bias defaults. Mitigation: pipeline requires a min-sample-size config and will skip tenants with insufficient samples. Risk: quant rollouts that degrade quality. Mitigation: strict safety gates, operator signoff, and canary promotion mode (thriftyctl supports canary pre-promotions). Related work: RFC-1227 'Defaults as Code' and ENG-4920.
